findings.title: Automatic confirmation no longer rearms failed or revoked admission scopes
Late verification cannot overwrite concurrent revocation under the current record CAS
Unscoped legacy drafts are isolated from cross-workspace save, rebind, and delete
Handoff grouping preserves distinct target activations and unknown receivers
Provider-reported cost is shown separately from tokens and any verified bill

limitations: User personal UX acceptance remains pending; Codex-operated Chromium and native sessions are technical evidence, not user approval.

The candidate is a read-only frozen export without .git. Independent reconstruction matched the supplied 194-file candidate SHA-256 and Git tree; the bounded hash check matched all 75 evidence-manifest entries.

The supplied same-candidate regression evidence records 650 Python tests, browser/HTTP suites, syntax, privacy, and byte-identical build checks as passing. Independent focused JavaScript checks passed 56 tests and focused Python checks passed 56 of 57: the sole failure was the exact outer-bwrap filesystem test, blocked before assertions by this review kernel refusing unprivileged namespace creation. The bounded command was run as `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=tools:tests python3 -B -m unittest -v test_native_terminals.NativeTerminalOuterIsolationTests`; supplied host/native evidence covers the enforcement and actual native read-tool path, while current local namespace enforcement was not rerun.

Native evidence proves recorded requested/reported identities, UUID/cwd bindings, terminal behavior, and the actual read-tool result where supplied; physical backend and effective effort remain unknown, and reported Provider cost is not a verified bill.
The source audit did not read credentials, native transcripts, or hidden reasoning, and made no source, authority, commit, push, merge, Stable-promotion, or model-call changes.
